facts.fact: African Manager, citing the BCT's 2025 supervision report, says Tunisia had six authorised payment institutions at end-2025, five of them active, with a seventh in 2026, and that the BCT issued circular 2026-10 on payment account rules.

TUN.note: Document states nothing on consumer rules, complaints or enforcement.
Diaspora inflows are mentioned but no named corridor or regional link.
Document states nothing on government payments to people.

facts.fact: The BCT's circular no. 2026-10 of 25 September 2026 raised payment-account ceilings (level 1 from 500 to 1,500 dinars, level 2 to 5,000, level 3 to 20,000), allowed remote opening and created an uncapped merchant account, per African Manager.
African Manager says the BCT's report covers non-bank payment institutions authorised to open payment accounts, six authorised at end-2025 with 113,739 accounts.

TUN.note: Only account counts from payment institutions, not a survey of adults.

facts.fact: Five payment institutions were active at end-2025 managing 113,739 payment accounts, 8.7 million transactions worth 3,775 MDT in 2025, per the BCT report as reported by African Manager.

TUN.note: Bill payments are mentioned but no tax or fee payment to the state.
